summary:
Lunar Archive — Explore Apollo Hardware is an interactive educational website that introduces visitors to important hardware left on the Moon during the Apollo missions. It explores three examples: the Lunar Module descent stage, the lunar laser retroreflector, and the Apollo seismometers.

The website explains what these pieces of equipment were, how they worked, and why they remain significant to lunar exploration and scientific research. Through interactive exhibits and a knowledge quiz, users can learn about the engineering achievements of the Apollo program and the scientific value of equipment left on the lunar surface.

The project aims to make Apollo-era technology and its lasting contributions easier to understand, especially for students and people interested in space exploration.
details:
Project Details

Lunar Archive — Explore Apollo Hardware is an interactive educational website designed to help people discover and understand important equipment left on the Moon during NASA’s Apollo missions.

The project focuses on three Apollo-era technologies: the Lunar Module descent stage, the lunar laser retroreflector, and the Apollo seismometers. Each exhibit explains the purpose of the equipment, how it worked, and its importance to space exploration and scientific research.

The website makes information about Apollo hardware easier to explore through organized exhibits, clear explanations, and an interactive knowledge quiz. Instead of presenting information as ordinary text, it encourages visitors to explore each piece of equipment and test what they have learned.

The intended impact is to increase awareness of the engineering achievements of the Apollo missions and show how equipment from past lunar missions continues to contribute to scientific knowledge.

The project is creative because it presents historical lunar technology in an accessible, interactive format. It combines educational content with exploration and a quiz to make learning more engaging. The website is hosted on Netlify.
